newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court extends supplementary protection to all patent holders.
newsitem.headline: Court extends supplementary protection to all patent holders.

text.p: The European Court of Justice confirmed on Thursday Community rules permit all basic patent holders of medicinal products to receive supplementary protection certificates extending the length of the patent.

The court said firms marketing pharmaceutical products are not required under Community rules to provide patent holders with copies of an original marketing authorization, but that obligation may be agreed to under contract.

The court said member states cannot refuse to extend patent protection to product developers unable to obtain copies of the original marketing authorization, if the basic patent and marketing authorizations are held by different persons.

These issues were resolved in the context of a dispute between Biogen and Smithkline Beecham's (SKB) Belgian operations. SKB, the marketer of Engerix-B, a vaccine against Hepatitis B, did not supply Biogen with a copy of its marketing authorization in Belgium. SKB did provide a copy of such authorization to the Institut Pasteur.
Biogen and the Institut Pasteur both hold patents relevant to the production of Engerix-B.

Biogen commenced an action in Belgium claiming SKB acted contrary to fair business practice rules under Belgian law. The Belgian court asked for an interpretation of the Community regulation enacted to protect the research and development investments put into pharmaceutical product development.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
Reference from the Tribunal de Commerce, Nivelles (Belgium) for a ruling in the case between
on the interpretation of Council regulation (EEC) No 1768/92 of 18 June 1992 concerning the creation of a supplementary protection certificate for medicinal products (OJ1992 L 182,p 1)

1. Where a medicinal product is covered by several basic patents, Council regulation (EEC) No 1768/92 of 18 June 1992 concerning the creation of a supplementary protection certificate for medicinal products does not preclude the grant of a supplementary protection certificate to each holder of a basic patent.
2. Regulation No 1768/92 does not require the holder of the marketing authorization to provide the patent holder with a copy of that authorization, referred to in article 8(1)(b) of the regulation.

3. Where the basic patent and the authorization to place the product on the market as a medicinal product are held by different persons and the patent holder is unable to provide a copy of that authorization in accordance with article 8(1)1(b) of regulation No 1768/92, an application for a certificate must not be refused on that ground alone.
